keyFindings.description: The operator README states the issue's outcome as fact — "Above one replica the app rolls instead: a new pod is ready before an old one stops, and its readers see no gap" — but the rendering does not support it. No pod template in this change carries a lifecycle/preStop (grep for `lifecycle` over packages/envoy/infra/gcp/ and the three goldens finds none), and cmd/dispatch/shutdown.go:88 calls server.Shutdown(context.Background()) as soon as SIGTERM arrives, which closes the listening socket at once while EndpointSlice removal is asynchronous, so a connection that lands on a terminating pod in the propagation window is reset. The tester recorded exactly this as unproven in .legion/INFRA-62/test.json (unproven[0] item 3 and unproven[1]'s closing sentence, which names this same README clause). Fix: either give envoy-dispatch a preStop delay and re-prove the rollout, or say what the rollout does guarantee (capacity is kept) and name the residual.

TestDispatchNetworkPolicyAdmitsOnlyTheGivenNamespaces reads spec.ingress[0] alone, so in the allowedNamespaces shape the consuming stack actually uses (envoy, legion) nothing asserts that the front-door rule is still present. Replacing the append at dispatch_kube.go:344 with an assignment inside the `if len(args.AllowedNamespaces) > 0` block would keep the whole suite green while leaving Tailscale Serve unable to reach the app at any port — a total outage, invisible to CI, in the one configuration production runs. policyIngressPods (dispatch_test.go:521) requires len(ingress)==1 and so cannot cover this case. Acceptance 1 asks for the front-door arrangement asserted rather than described; it is asserted only at the default. Fix: assert both rules (count and the front-door peer) in that test.

The front-door recreate is described as "Serve is down while the tailnet pod is replaced", but the app's readiness reads NATS (cmd/dispatch/main.go:969, ok := databaseOK && (natsOK == nil || *natsOK)) and NATS reaches the hub only through that proxy, so every app replica fails its readiness probe and leaves Service <hostname> too. The in-cluster allowedNamespaces path goes down with Serve, not just the tailnet path. Self-healing (internal/bus/nats.go sets MaxReconnect = -1, and there is no liveness probe), and not a regression from the base, but the sentence understates the blast radius.

The CI line attaches the wrong workflow names to the run ids: 39513347754 is `Legion Envoy and Contracts`, 39513347783 is `Tests`, and 39513347690 is `Docs` (gh run view at each id). The job lists and the head SHA are right; only the names are swapped.

The body carries no `## Contract change census` though the change adds a refusal at a process boundary (`replicas %d must be at least %d`, dispatch.go:266, raised through the Construct RPC). Its population is empty — the input is new in this PR, so no existing consumer can reach the refusal, and no program in this repository sets DispatchArgs.Replicas — and the rollout is an immediate refusal, which is right because the value it closes (replicas 0) would take Dispatch to zero pods silently. Record that in a short census section rather than leaving it unstated.

thermonuclear.deepReview: No blocking correctness or security defect. Verified no issue: the listener bearer wired end to end (RandomPassword <h>-listener-token -> Secret <h>-listener/ENVOY_API_TOKEN -> listener ENVOY_API_TOKEN and app ENVOY_TOKEN -> internal/dispatch/envoy/client.go's Authorization: Bearer); /healthz and /metrics being auth-exempt widens nothing, since NetworkPolicy <h>-listener admits 9020 from app=<h> alone and the probe is exec on loopback; Tailscale Serve dialling a cluster DNS name is sound against upstream ipn/ipnlocal/serve.go (SystemDial, no loopback restriction on the TS_SERVE_CONFIG path); no deadlock or crash-loop in the DependsOn chain; Recreate vs RollingUpdate right per workload; nothing in the diff replaces a resource (name, namespace and selector of Deployment <h> unchanged). Two Medium findings raised, both carried into this review (the README's gapless claim and the cutover's two tailscaled processes, the latter already placed in INFRA-63's spec).
thermonuclear.codeQuality: Component contract followed (resolve -> require -> register, the refusal naming its input with both a resolver row and a Construct row, plain *int with its output-refusal test, goldens regenerated beside their tests). One major finding, carried as the fast-follow: the strategy rule (1 -> Recreate, above 1 -> RollingUpdate{0,1}) is encoded in four places — dispatchStrategy/dispatchRollingUpdate/dispatchStrategyFor in dispatch.go, deploymentStrategy in dispatch_kube.go, and DispatchRollingUpdate in export_test.go — with no branch anywhere switching on strategyType. Judged not blocking: it is duplication, not a defect, and the rendered-Deployment tests already pin both cases.
